notes: Feng Office SQL injection in MoreController update_system_module_order/update_dimension_order via modules/dims argument. No poc_refs; the only PoC is a Google Drive PDF that cannot be fetched, and no accessible source gives the concrete URL path or request shape. Feng Office uses an index.php?c=<controller>&a=<action> routing convention, but the exact route for MoreController could not be confirmed, so building would require guessing the path. Feng Office SQL injection in Legacy API Contacts::instance->findAll (CompanyWebsite.class.php) via auth argument. No poc_refs; the only PoC is a Google Drive PDF that cannot be fetched. No accessible source gives the concrete URL path/route or request shape for the legacy API 'auth' parameter, so building would require guessing the endpoint. Per spec, dropped rather than invent an endpoint.

SQL injection in OpenPanel analytics filter builder via a profile.* filter column identifier. The GHSA/VulnCheck advisories name the entry path (GET /insights/:projectId/events and sibling insights endpoints) but deliberately withhold any PoC and do not document how analytics filters are serialized onto the request (query string vs JSON body, exact filter-object encoding). The injection is in a column identifier inside a filter 'name' field; building a faithful request would require guessing the request encoding, so dropped per spec.

NoSQL injection (CWE-943) in the MongoDB integration for Laravel: the three-argument where method with '='/'eq', and the find/delete methods on that path, can interpret an operator-shaped array as a query condition. This is a library-level flaw with no fixed HTTP endpoint or parameter; exploitation depends entirely on how a consuming application wires user input into these APIs. No concrete path+parameter to target, so no faithful WAF request can be built.

Unauthenticated SQL injection in the Yo WordPress plugin (<=1.3.1) via the username request parameter. WPScan and Wordfence both withhold the PoC ('displayed once remediated'), and neither the advisories nor plugin searches reveal the exact endpoint (AJAX action name / admin-ajax.php action / REST route) carrying the username parameter. Parameter name alone (username) is insufficient; building would require guessing the path/action, so dropped.

Unauthenticated SQL injection in the Tz Weekly Radio Schedule WordPress plugin (tz-wrs-core <=1.8.1) via an AJAX action. The WPScan PoC is withheld; the vulnerability name references the action tzwrs_update_cell, but the exact injectable parameter name is not published and could not be recovered (plugin SVN trunk listings redirect to http and did not resolve). Guessing the parameter would fail condition 2, so dropped.

Tz Weekly Radio Schedule WordPress plugin (tz-wrs-core) <=1.8.1 unauthenticated SQLi on an AJAX action. WPScan PoC is withheld ('displayed once remediated', no known fix) and names no AJAX action; the WPScan title hints the 'week' parameter but the admin-ajax.php action is not disclosed. Wordfence page is JS-rendered (no extractable detail) and plugin SVN source is unreachable via the agent proxy. Cannot determine the exact action without guessing, so condition 2 fails.

Product Question and Answer WordPress plugin <=1.1.0 unauthenticated SQLi on AJAX actions. WPScan PoC withheld; neither the AJAX action name nor the exact parameter is disclosed. Wordfence page is JS-rendered and plugin SVN source is unreachable via the agent proxy. Building a faithful admin-ajax.php request would require guessing the action/parameter, so condition 2 fails.

Price Drop Alert for WooCommerce WordPress plugin (woo-price-drop-alert) <=1.1 unauthenticated SQLi on an AJAX action. WPScan PoC withheld; no AJAX action name or parameter disclosed. Wordfence/Sentinelone pages carry no request detail and plugin SVN source is unreachable via the agent proxy. Cannot build without guessing the action/parameter, so condition 2 fails.

'wp shortcut link and advertisement baner' WordPress plugin <=1.2.0 unauthenticated SQLi on an AJAX action. WPScan PoC withheld; no AJAX action name or parameter disclosed. No Wordfence/threat-intel page with request detail located and plugin SVN source is unreachable via the agent proxy. Cannot build without guessing the action/parameter, so condition 2 fails.

SQL injection lives in the llmware Python library's collection-database layer (llmware/resources.py). The tainted filter/lookup values reach the sink only through in-process Python API calls (Library.block_lookup, Query.text_query_with_custom_filter, Query.text_query_by_author_or_speaker); llmware ships no HTTP server exposing these, so there is no inbound server-side HTTP request to simulate. Per SPEC 3.4, library/Python API injections are dropped.

n8n Elasticsearch/Firestore query injection is a workflow node EXPRESSION injection (PR:L, attacker edits a workflow). The advisory names no inbound HTTP route, path or parameter against n8n itself; the malicious value is interpolated inside a node's query field, not sent as a WAF-inspectable request. No faithful server-side HTTP request can be built.

AVideo get.json.php APIName=channels sort injection is an ORDER BY identifier/column oracle: the endpoint's character filter strips quotes, parentheses and commas, so only bare identifiers like u.password pass. The faithful exploit payload (a column name) carries no WAF-detectable attack signature, and any classic SQLi signature would not match the real (filtered) attack. Fails condition 1.

MikroORM is a Node.js/TypeScript ORM library. The orderBy direction SQL injection occurs inside em.find()/QueryBuilder.orderBy() when an application binds attacker input to the direction value. There is no fixed HTTP path or parameter - it depends entirely on the consuming application. No faithful CVE-specific request can be built without guessing an endpoint.

Kirki WordPress plugin (6.0.0-6.2.5) Editor+ SQL injection via a 'Content Manager Field ID' identifier. WPScan withheld the PoC and neither WPScan, Wordfence, Patchstack nor the Lutra field guide disclose the concrete endpoint (admin-ajax action or REST route), parameter name, or payload. Building would require guessing the path/parameter, which the spec forbids.
waf_rules_found: Wordfence and Patchstack advisories indicate generic SQLi mitigation rules exist but neither publishes the request path/parameter.

notes: wp-review-slider-pro < 12.7.12 stored SQLi via an AJAX handler lacking a capability check. The WPScan PoC is withheld ('displayed once remediated') and neither the Wordfence entry, OpenCVE nor the CVE record names the exact parameter or AJAX action. Only a 'Stored Template Filter' hint is given. Cannot determine the exact parameter/action without guessing, so dropped per spec condition 2.

NextGen Connect (Mirth Connect) <=4.7.1: an authenticated user can execute arbitrary SQL through the Database Connector API. This is abuse of a feature that legitimately sends SQL to connected databases, not injection via a specific request parameter. No advisory/PoC/WAF rule gives a concrete inbound HTTP path, parameter, and injectable payload, so no faithful CVE-tied, signature-bearing request can be built. The securityarsenal guide only offers generic SQLi detection heuristics (UNION SELECT / SLEEP( on /api/, /webadmin/, /services/mirth), not an exploit-derived request.

ILIAS repository trash table SQL injection via the table navigation sort field (ORDER BY). The VulnCheck advisory and the researcher advisory (SIT-2026-001) explicitly state they contain no ready-to-use PoC and no payloads. Only the value format 'field:direction:offset' is given; the exact HTTP parameter name, the baseClass/cmdClass/cmd route, and the trash-table GET parameter name are not published. Building a request would require guessing the parameter name, which the spec forbids.

WPvivid Backup, Migration & Staging < 0.9.133 admin SQL injection via an unsanitised user-supplied list of identifiers. The WPScan advisory withholds the PoC and does not name the vulnerable AJAX action/endpoint or the exact parameter. No other source (fieldguide, opencve, hol.org) names a concrete path+parameter. Admin-only, medium severity. Building would require guessing the parameter, which the spec forbids.

IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 SQLi in the Analytic Grid Service Handler (analytic cases grid endpoint). Closed-source enterprise product; only an IBM bulletin exists, naming the component but giving no concrete URL path, parameter name, HTTP method, or PoC. Cannot build a faithful request without inventing the endpoint/parameter.

Mislabeled as SQLi; actually stored DOM-based XSS in Concrete CMS Gallery block per-image Caption field. The caption is attribute-encoded on storage and only executes client-side when the Magnific Popup lightbox re-parses it via jQuery .append() (titleSrc). No public PoC or documented storing endpoint/parameter for the block-edit request; only vendor release notes. Payload is not present as raw HTML in an inbound request, so no WAF-blockable server-side signature could be built faithfully.

IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 SQLi in the New Query Builder REST Processor (newQueryBuilder REST endpoint). Closed-source; only the IBM bulletin exists, naming the processor but giving no concrete URL path, injectable parameter, method, or PoC. Cannot build without guessing.

IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 unauthenticated SQLi in the Load Balancer Groups component (Load Balancer Servlet / LBServlet). Closed-source; IBM bulletin and third-party write-ups mention 'LBServlet' but give no concrete path, injectable parameter name, method, or PoC request. Cannot build a faithful request without inventing the parameter.

MongoDB PHP client library (mongo-php-library / mongo-php-driver) does not sanitize application-supplied namespace identifiers. This is a library-level flaw: it only manifests if an application passes untrusted text into namespace identifiers. No defined inbound HTTP endpoint, path, or request parameter exists to target, and no attack-signature payload applies. Not a server-side inbound HTTP request.

Craft CMS GraphQL entry mutation (saveEntry/deleteEntry) reads siteId without site-scope filtering, letting a token scoped to Site A act on Site B. Mislabeled as SQL injection; it is an authorization/site-scope bypass. The exploit only passes a normal integer siteId in a GraphQL mutation - there is no malicious attack signature (no SQLi/XSS/traversal payload) that a WAF would block. Fails condition 1.

CakePHP framework library flaw: FunctionsBuilder::cast/extract/datePart/dateAdd in src/Database/FunctionsBuilder.php accept user-controlled dataType/part/unit and incorporate them as unescaped SQL fragments. This is a framework API issue that only manifests if an application passes untrusted input to these builder methods. No defined inbound HTTP endpoint, path, or parameter. Not a server-side inbound HTTP request.

WP Ultimate CSV Importer SQL injection requires an authenticated administrator to upload a CSV whose cell (mapped to the All in One SEO seo_title field) contains a SQL subquery. The injection lives inside an uploaded CSV file processed through the multi-step admin import wizard; no concrete single HTTP endpoint/path or request parameter is documented, and CRS/ModSecurity does not inspect uploaded file contents by default. Cannot faithfully reconstruct one inbound request with a named parameter; fails condition 2.

ash_sql is an Elixir library (AshSql.Expr). The bug is a self-defeating LIKE-wildcard escape helper reached through contains/2, string_starts_with/2, string_ends_with/2 - a library API, not a specific inbound HTTP endpoint/parameter. The value stays parameterized (confined to LIKE pattern grammar, not full SQL), so there is no real SQL-injection signature to place and no concrete path+parameter. CWE-943 but not expressible as a WAF-blockable web request.

WP Project Manager Pro (wedevs) authenticated subscriber SQL injection. No public PoC available (SentinelOne: 'No verified public proof-of-concept code is available'). Wordfence advisory page returns empty content and names no parameter; NVD/OpenCVE give no concrete endpoint or vulnerable parameter. Advisory only says 'user-supplied parameter' used in an AJAX/REST query. Cannot determine exact path+parameter without guessing, so dropped per spec section 5.

ash_sqlite is an Elixir/Ash data-layer library. The flaw is in AshSqlite.SqlImplementation building a SQLite json_extract path from a get_path/2 segment; the path is bound as a parameter and the issue is confined to the JSON-path grammar (not SQL injection). No concrete server-side HTTP endpoint or parameter exists - exploitability depends entirely on an unknown consuming application's 'pick-a-field' endpoint. Library-level, no fixed path/parameter to build a faithful request. Advisory itself says this is not SQL but JSON-path traversal.

CakePHP framework-level issue: FunctionsBuilder::jsonValue() with PostgresDriver is injectable when user data reaches the jsonPath argument. This is a PHP framework API, not a concrete inbound HTTP request - there is no fixed path or request parameter. Exploitability depends on an unknown application passing user input into jsonValue(). No path/parameter to build a request tied to the CVE.

The authoritative PoC gist describes a CWE-20 array-coercion input-validation bug in POST /public/submit.php (person[0][]=...), NOT SQL injection: the insert uses a prepared statement with bind_param('s', $person) and a nested array is coerced to the literal string 'Array' and stored. No 'Researcher' parameter and no injectable SQL signature exist. CWE-89 over-labels the bug; trusting the PoC there is no attack signature a WAF would/should block.

WordPress egoi Smart Marketing plugin 'SQL injection via Parameter Name'. The vulnerable listener (class-egoi-for-wp-listener.php) is not a dedicated plugin endpoint; it is invoked via init($user_id) from an internal WordPress hook (user registration / profile / WooCommerce checkout) and merges all $_POST keys (array_merge($_POST,...)) into a query via get_default_map(). The injection is in the parameter NAME, not value, and no public source identifies the exact HTTP endpoint/URL that triggers it. Wordfence advisory page returned empty; trac is robots-disallowed. Building would require guessing the trigger endpoint, which the spec forbids.

TYPO3 extension 'Forms Export' (frp_form_answers / frappant) SQL injection in a backend module. The advisory does not name the injectable URL parameter, the backend module route, or the HTTP method, and no public PoC exists. TYPO3 backend modules require an authenticated backend session and a valid module route token, so the exact path+parameter cannot be reconstructed from public sources. Entry point not recoverable.

n8n Supabase node PostgREST filter injection. This is a workflow-node configuration/expression-resolution issue, not an inbound HTTP request to a fixed n8n endpoint. The GHSA advisory names no HTTP path, parameter, or request format; exploitation depends on a workflow routing untrusted input (e.g. via a webhook trigger) into a manual-filter Supabase operation. No concrete path+parameter to tie a WAF request to the CVE.

n8n MongoDB node NoSQL injection ($ne/$where via resolved Query expression). This is a workflow-node configuration/expression-resolution issue, not an inbound HTTP request to a fixed n8n endpoint. The GHSA advisory names no HTTP path or parameter; exploitation depends on a workflow placing externally-controlled data into the MongoDB node Query field. No concrete path+parameter to tie a WAF request to the CVE.

GeoTools is a Java geospatial library. SQLi is in the jsonArrayContains OGC filter function (PostGIS DataStore). The advisory, PR and commit give no concrete HTTP request, endpoint path or parameter; GeoTools itself exposes no HTTP surface. Reaching it would require guessing a GeoServer WFS/CQL_FILTER endpoint, which the spec forbids.

baserCMS SQLi in BcDatabaseService.php is triggered through a multi-step backup-restore chain: the attacker plants malicious table names via a schema-file ZIP uploaded during restore, then error-based SQLi fires on later operations. The VulnCheck advisory gives no single HTTP request with an injectable parameter and value; the only direct-POST point (deleteTables schema) has no confirmed endpoint/parameter. Not expressible as one inbound request with a signature in a named parameter.

Fabrik (Joomla extension) unauthenticated SQLi in the list ORDER BY via an 'order' parameter with a CONCAT( allowlist bypass. No public PoC; advisories name the attack class but not the exact Joomla request structure (com_fabrik list view id, how the order var is packaged in the request). Building would require guessing the parameter packaging and listid, which the spec forbids.

Fabrik (Joomla extension) unauthenticated SQLi in the list filter 'condition' parameter concatenated into the WHERE clause (getFilterQuery). No public PoC; advisories give no concrete HTTP request, no com_fabrik list id and no exact request-var naming for the condition parameter. Exact entry point cannot be reconstructed without guessing.

WP Import Export Lite < 3.9.33 SQLi via export filter values. WPScan advisory withholds the PoC (scheduled for 2026-09-28) and gives no endpoint, parameter name or payload. Unlike its sibling CVE-2026-76557 (import), no entry point is public, so it cannot be tied to a concrete parameter without guessing.
Cisco ISE API SQLi; vendor PSIRT advisory names no concrete endpoint path or parameter, no PoC. Cannot build a CVE-tied request.
Splunk SOAR SQLi via custom function results / DB lookup name; advisory gives no REST endpoint path or parameter, no PoC.
Splunk Enterprise Data Orchestration jobs SQLi; advisory (SVD-2026-0801) names no concrete REST path or parameter, no PoC.
Splunk Enterprise SPL injection via saved-search dispatch time values; no concrete path/parameter in advisory and SPL is not a standard WAF signature class.
stigmem-node Postgres schema-identifier SQLi is an internal/library code path; schema value is operator-controlled from deployment config, not an inbound HTTP parameter. No endpoint.

Marten is a .NET document-DB/ORM library. The SQL injection is in internal LINQ/tenant-management code paths (DictionaryItemMember.cs, SelectParser.cs, DatabaseScopedTenantPartitions.cs, etc.) reached via library API calls such as Where filters and IEventStore.DeleteProjectionProgressAsync. There is no fixed inbound HTTP endpoint or request parameter; the tainted input is a dictionary indexer key supplied through the .NET API, not an HTTP request. Not expressible as a WAF webRequest.

GraphQL query injection in the Rapid7 Bulk Export MCP server (get_export_status, export_manager.py). The injectable export_id arrives as an MCP tool argument from an MCP client (or indirect prompt injection), not as an inbound HTTP request to the vulnerable component; the resulting GraphQL document is sent OUTBOUND to Rapid7's API under the operator's own API key. There is no server-side inbound HTTP endpoint/parameter a WAF could inspect, and it grants no access beyond the operator's existing authenticated scope.

Library-level NoSQL/aggregation-expression injection in the MongoDB-for-Laravel cache lock implementation: a caller-supplied lock 'owner' value is evaluated as an aggregation expression. The owner value is set by the consuming application's own code (Laravel cache lock API), so there is no fixed HTTP endpoint, path or request parameter to target; the vector depends entirely on how a downstream app wires user input into the lock owner. No public PoC request, path or parameter. label_confidence was low.

Authenticated Contao-backend SQL injection in several Isotope eCommerce backend callbacks (Attribute/Callback.php onLoad/validateForeignKey, ProductPrice/Callback.php, MediaManager.php) that interpolate request-controlled identifiers and admin-supplied values. The VulnCheck advisory and GitHub issue #2585 intentionally omit a weaponized PoC and do not pin the concrete backend route (the Contao do= module) or request parameter; building a faithful request would require guessing the backend module path and parameter. Per spec, dropped rather than guess the entry point.

SQL injection is triggered via a crafted SIP From header (Caller ID name) on an inbound SIP call to a monitored extension, inserted by agi-bin/missedcallnotify.php. It is not reachable by an inbound HTTP request, so no webRequest can simulate it.

SQLi is delivered through a crafted MySQL table NAME (backtick + stacked statement) that executes when a Budibase admin later runs schema discovery (DESCRIBE). The injection payload lives in a database object name, not in any parameter of the triggering inbound HTTP request, so there is no WAF-inspectable attack signature on the wire.

Advisory (GHSA-q6x4-v3qx-85qw) describes MySQL multipleStatements:true but its only PoC is a Node.js mysql2 script connecting directly to the database. No HTTP endpoint, path or request parameter is named, and the description only says 'user input fields' generically. Cannot tie a payload to a concrete inbound request.

PeerTube SQLi in ActorFollowModel.updateScore via actor inboxUrl. The injected value (inboxUrl) is read from a remote ActivityPub actor document that PeerTube fetches server-side during federation, not supplied in a WAF-inspectable parameter of the inbound inbox/follow request. Fix commit confirms inboxUrl string interpolation but no inbound HTTP parameter carries the payload.

ERPNext SQLi sink is get_tax_template(posting_date, args) in tax_rule.py, confirmed string-interpolating posting_date into a WHERE clause. But get_tax_template is NOT @frappe.whitelist() (verified in source); it is only reached internally. No advisory/PoC names the whitelisted HTTP endpoint and parameter that carry attacker-controlled posting_date, so building a request would require inventing the entry point.

Metabase SQLi via a public card/dashboard field-filter (dimension) parameter. The GHSA advisory gives no endpoint path, no card/dashboard UUID handling and no field-filter parameter name, and no public PoC exists. Cannot place a payload in a confirmed path+parameter.

Metabase SQLi via POST /api/session/reset_password is known at endpoint level, but the root cause (per Bishop Fox / VulnCheck) is failure to restrict UNDECLARED fields in the reset body, not classic string concatenation, and the specific injectable field name is not public (no PoC released). Cannot place a signature payload in a confirmed parameter.

Budibase Oracle connector SQLi via unescaped table name in a post-write row lookup. Exploitation requires an Oracle table whose NAME contains a double-quote; the payload is the DB object name, consumed server-side during the lookup, and is not present in any parameter of the inbound HTTP request, so no WAF-inspectable attack signature exists on the wire.

Second-order SQLi via attribute-view template columns (queryBlocks). Advisory states AV mutations are admin-gated, so an unauthenticated inbound request cannot plant the payload; exploitation requires distributing a crafted SiYuan document/package that a victim imports and renders. No direct inbound HTTP request with an attack signature in a named parameter; the performTransactions injection path is not even fully given by the advisory. Delivered via a malicious document, not a web request.

SQLi in the n8n PostgresTrigger node: user-supplied identifier params (channel/function/trigger names) are interpolated into SQL run against the connected external PostgreSQL. The injection lives deep inside workflow node configuration JSON set by an authenticated workflow author; there is no public PoC HTTP request and no fixed path+parameter a WAF in front of n8n would inspect. Cannot build a faithful request without guessing the workflow/node structure.

SQLi in the n8n Snowflake node Execute Query operation: untrusted expression data is interpolated into a raw SQL string executed against external Snowflake. Injection is in workflow node config set by a workflow author, not a fixed inbound HTTP path+parameter. No public PoC request; building one would require guessing the workflow node JSON. Not a WAF-testable inbound request.

SQLi in Tencent APIJSON via the Map-form @having operator. Advisory confirms the String-form is NOT vulnerable and only the Map-form triggers it, but no PoC and no public description of the exact Map-form JSON structure/key that carries the injection. Building a request would require guessing the nested JSON shape of the vulnerable @having map. No entry point confirmable.

SQLi in Pimcore admin-ui-classic-bundle DataObject grid 'id column filter'. No public PoC and no confirmed admin endpoint path or the exact filter JSON parameter structure (grid-proxy filter array). Authenticated backend only. Cannot build a faithful request without guessing the endpoint and the filter condition format.

SQLi in CiviCRM contact search 'RLIKE clause'. Advisory names only the component, not the exact AJAX/search endpoint or the request parameter carrying the RLIKE value. Authenticated staff only. No PoC found; building a request would require guessing both the endpoint and the parameter.

SQLi in e107 2.4.0 'news item page ID parameter'. CVE names neither the exact URL (news.php logic lives in e107_plugins/news/news.php and parses e_QUERY) nor the exact GET parameter. No public PoC or fix commit found; news.php only includes the plugin. Cannot confirm the exact path+parameter without guessing.

Stored SQLi in Koha via the image_name field of a patron card layout; the value is stored verbatim in layout XML and later concatenated into SQL in patroncards/create-pdf.pl at print time. Per spec, the WAF request must be the STORING request (the layout save), but the exact layout-editor endpoint and its POST field name are not confirmable (vendor bugzilla is access-restricted via Anubis; no public PoC). Cannot build the storing request without guessing. The create-pdf.pl request itself carries no payload (stored value).

Vulnerability is in the drogon C++ ORM library function makeCriteria (orm_lib/src/Criteria.cc), argument filter. It is a library-level SQL injection with no specific application HTTP path or parameter; exploitation depends on whatever app uses the ORM. No inbound HTTP entry point is named, so no faithful request can be built (spec library/API exclusion).

Vulnerability is in the drogon C++ ORM library function Mapper::orderBy (Mapper.h), argument sort. Library-level SQL injection with no specific application HTTP path or parameter; depends on the consuming app. No inbound HTTP entry point named, so no faithful request can be built.

Despite the CWE-89 label this is an unauthenticated arbitrary file deletion in the AcyMailing extension (Patchstack confirms Arbitrary File Deletion), not SQL injection. The deletion path is stored in a file-type custom field and triggered when the field is cleared; this is a logic flaw with no WAF-blockable injection signature and no published concrete HTTP request/parameter.

OpenPanel ClickHouse SQL injection via the filter name in series[].filters[].name (getSelectPropertyKey in chart.service.ts), PoC filter name "properties.x'] = 'never' OR 1=1 OR e.properties['x". The injection point and payload are known, but neither the GHSA advisory nor VulnCheck publish the concrete HTTP route or method (internal tRPC/API endpoint); the reproducer script contents are not public. Building would require guessing the path, which fails condition 2.

Better Messages WordPress plugin SQLi via 'group_id' Message Meta Parameter. Tracing the referenced source (inc/rest-api.php, functions.php, addons/buddyboss.php), group_id is read server-side from thread meta (get_thread_meta), not accepted as a direct request parameter on any confirmable REST route (namespace better-messages/v1). No PoC request available (Wordfence and Patchstack pages give no request details), and exploitation requires a specific BuddyBoss state. Could not determine the exact path+parameter+transport to carry a faithful SQLi signature without guessing, so dropped per spec.

Mongoid (MongoDB Ruby ODM library) NoSQL injection: library does not restrict which query operators come from caller-supplied filter data when handed to its query-building methods. This is a library-level flaw (CWE-943) with no fixed HTTP endpoint, path or parameter; the entry point depends entirely on the consuming application's code. No PoC and no concrete inbound HTTP request can be built faithfully.

Snowflake CLI is a command-line tool. Exploitation requires supplying a malicious project configuration file or crafted command-line input that the CLI interpolates into multi-statement SQL executed against the victim's Snowflake session. There is no inbound server-side HTTP request/endpoint to a WAF-protected host; the attack vector is a local config file / CLI argument in a CI/CD pipeline.

Sulu Smart Content QueryBuilder concatenates the public 'categories' query parameter into a JCR-SQL2 WHERE clause. The parameter name is known, but the advisory gives no concrete URL path: the injection triggers on 'any public page that renders a Smart Content element with category filtering enabled', which is site/content specific. Building a request would require guessing the page path, which the spec forbids. No PoC URL and no HTTP method provided.

Discourse 'NoSQL injection' (CWE-943) is actually unescaped SQL LIKE metacharacters (% and _ wildcards) in upload-resolution patterns, letting an authenticated user match unrelated upload records. The exploit payload is just wildcard characters, which is not a WAF-blockable attack signature (no XSS/SQLi/RCE pattern), and the advisory names no specific HTTP endpoint or parameter. Fails both condition 1 (no real signature) and condition 2 (no named entry point).

Booking Manager WordPress plugin SQLi is triggered via the UID field of a crafted external iCalendar (.ics) feed that the plugin fetches and parses server-side (shortcode [booking-manager-import url=...]). The malicious SQL (e.g. UID:x') OR SLEEP(5)-- -) lives in the externally fetched feed content, not in any inbound HTTP request parameter a WAF could inspect. No inbound request carries the attack signature, so a WAF rule on the request cannot block it.

orval is a build-time code generator. A single quote in an OpenAPI/Swagger schema property name is emitted into generated MSW mock factory code; code execution happens when that generated code is run/imported in a dev/CI/test environment, not via any inbound HTTP request to a running server. Advisory confirms the vector is 'generate mocks from an attacker-controlled spec and run them'. Not a server-side web request (spec section 3.4).

orval is a build-time code generator. A double quote in an OpenAPI/Swagger schema property name is emitted into a generated zod.object({...}) schema; code executes when the generated zod module is imported in a dev/CI/test environment. No inbound HTTP request carries the payload to a running web server. Same root cause as CVE-2026-71867. Not a server-side web request (spec section 3.4).

ApiAdmin v5.0.1 SQL injection 'via the User.php component'. The only PoC is a Notion page that renders solely via JavaScript and returns no content to a fetch; NVD/Mend/OpenCVE/fieldguide pages carry only the generic description with no route, HTTP method, or parameter. Cannot determine the exact endpoint/parameter without guessing, so cannot build a faithful request (spec section 5).

Magistrala message-readers SQL injection. The messages route is GET /channels/{chanID}/messages and decodeList reads many query params (order, dir, format, subtopic, protocol, comparator, ...). The current source interpolates only format (via pq.QuoteIdentifier, safe) and comparator (via ParseValueComparator); order/dir are hardcoded. The CVE text does not name which specific query parameter is the raw fmt.Sprintf sink, and multiple candidates exist, so the exact injectable parameter cannot be fixed without guessing. Dropped to avoid fabricating a parameter (spec conditions 2 / section 6.6).

Cacti ORDER BY SQL injection rooted in the weak sanitize_sql_column regex in lib/functions.php (allows letters/digits/underscore/parens/dot so expressions pass unmodified). The advisory describes only the shared sanitizer function, not any specific page or request parameter. sanitize_sql_column is called from many scripts with varying sort_column-style parameters; selecting one endpoint/parameter would be a guess. No concrete path+parameter, so dropped (spec section 5, low label_confidence).

ChirpStack device tag-filtering SQL injection is SQLite-only (#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]) in chirpstack/src/storage/device.rs, where the tag map KEY (Filters.tags HashMap) is interpolated via format! into a raw SQL fragment. The sink is confirmed, but the storage layer is driven by the gRPC API and the source does not show which gRPC/REST method or request field populates Filters.tags with an attacker-controlled key; no reachable HTTP route+parameter could be confirmed. Expressing a faithful inbound HTTP request is not possible without guessing (spec conditions 2 / section 5).

Ghidra BSim SQL injection is reached via the BSim network query protocol (a Ghidra client/server database protocol over its own FunctionDatabase connection, not inbound HTTP). Filter values are sent to the BSim server and concatenated into PostgreSQL queries. There is no HTTP request path/parameter to simulate for a WAF.

MikroORM identifier-quoting / JSON-path helpers fail to escape delimiters when application code passes attacker-influenced identifier/JSON-property strings to public ORM APIs. It is a Node.js library API, not an HTTP endpoint; no fixed path/parameter. Not an inbound web request.

sequelize is a Node.js ORM library. The bug is in the internal escape() in sql-string.js for the Oracle dialect (values starting with TO_TIMESTAMP/TO_DATE are returned unescaped). ash-project/ash keyset pagination deserialization. AzuraCast backup restore. The 'azuracast:restore' console (CLI) command executes the db.sql file from a backup archive with no validation. n8n Snowflake / legacy MySQL v1 node SQLi. n8n Oracle DB node select 'Limit' field SQLi. The injectable Limit value comes from workflow expressions (optionally fed by a webhook), not a fixed HTTP path/parameter. No stable inbound request shape to build a signature-tied request.

Spring Data MongoDB library flaw: @Query regex parameter binding performs insufficient validation, allowing regex-quoting breakout (NoSQL injection). Spring AI RedisChatMemoryRepository.findByMetadata() RediSearch injection is a Java library method; the metadata value is a caller-supplied API argument, not an inbound HTTP parameter. No HTTP endpoint defined by the component.

TYPO3 Apache Solr extension: logic flaw where a request-provided additionalFilters parameter registers a named siteHash filter before the system's own, letting a visitor read another site's public documents in a shared Solr core. There is no inbound HTTP request to a web endpoint; it is a library-level issue not expressible as a WAF web request.

StoneFly Storage Concentrator cookie-based SQL injection via login.pl and debug.pl. langchain-mongodb / langgraph is a library. Unauthenticated SQL injection via the login field, but ProjeQtor's login endpoint (tool/loginCheck.php, reached by POSTing login+password submitted from the login form to the main app frame) AES-CTR decrypts the login value server-side before use: $login=AesCtr::decrypt($_POST['login'], $_SESSION['sessionSalt'], ...). DQL (Dgraph Query Language) injection via a JSON mutation key language tag to /mutate?commitNow=true (plus a /alter setup request). DQL (Dgraph Query Language) injection via the cond field of an upsert mutation in a single POST /mutate?commitNow=true. Frappe HR SQL injection 'due to improper field sanitization'. phpMyFAQ searchCustomPages LIKE-clause wildcard injection: real_escape_string fails to escape only the LIKE metacharacters % and _, so the attacker injects wildcards into a search term. % and _ are ordinary characters with no WAF-blockable attack signature (no quotes, UNION, or SQL operators pass), so no request a WAF would block can be built.

PraisonAI second-order SQLi in get_all_user_threads (f-string).
